claim: A single intranasal immunization of inactivated whole cell of Acinetobacter baumannii elicits rapid protection against broad A. baumannii-infected pneumonia via training of innate immune response in Rag1-/- mice.
source: Here, we demonstrated that a single intranasal immunization of inactivated whole cell of Acinetobacter baumannii elicits rapid protection against broad A. baumannii-infected pneumonia via training of innate immune response in Rag1-/- mice.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript including survival studies in Rag1-/- mice.

claim: Immunization-trained alveolar macrophages (AMs) showed enhanced TNF-α production upon restimulation.
source: Immunization-trained alveolar macrophages (AMs) showed enhanced TNF-α production upon restimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3B, 5C, and 5D showing increased TNF-α levels.

claim: Adoptive transfer of immunization-trained AMs into naive mice mediated rapid protection against infection.
source: Adoptive transfer of immunization-trained AMs into naive mice mediated rapid protection against infection.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5E showing reduced bacterial burdens and clinical scores.

claim: Elevated TLR4 expression on vaccination-trained AMs contributed to rapid protection.
source: Elevated TLR4 expression on vaccination-trained AMs contributed to rapid protection.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6 showing elevated TLR4 expression and reduced protection in Tlr4-/- mice.

claim: Immunization-induced rapid protection was observed in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia models.
source: Moreover, immunization-induced rapid protection was also seen in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia models, but not in Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae model.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by survival data in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Immunization-induced rapid protection was not observed in Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae pneumonia models.
source: Moreover, immunization-induced rapid protection was also seen in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia models, but not in Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae model.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by survival data in Figure 7C and 7D showing no significant protection.

claim: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria pose a great threat to global public health.
source: The multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, including Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus, pose a great threat to global public health (Tacconelli et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tacconelli et al., 2018.

claim: Pneumonia caused by MDR bacteria is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, especially in hospitalized patients.
source: Pneumonia caused by MDR bacteria is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, especially in hospitalized patients (Gonzalez-Villoria and Valverde-Garduno, 2016; Micek et al., 2015; Zilberberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies.

claim: Vaccination has been proposed as a promising strategy for controlling MDR bacterial infections.
source: Vaccination has been proposed as a promising strategy for controlling MDR bacterial infections (Jansen et al., 2018; Rappuoli et al., 2017; Williams, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies.

claim: Current vaccination strategies usually require multiple injections weeks or months apart.
source: Current vaccination strategies usually require multiple injections weeks or months apart, which limit them to rapidly prevent infections for inpatients.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about current vaccination approaches.

claim: Hospitalized patients have an especially high risk for exposure to MDR bacteria.
source: However, hospitalized patients have an especially high risk for exposure to MDR bacteria (Pachón and McConnell, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pachón and McConnell, 2014.

claim: Rapid efficacy induced by vaccination is vital for vaccine development against MDR bacteria.
source: Therefore, rapid efficacy induced by vaccination is vital for vaccine development against MDR bacteria (Pachón and McConnell, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited reference and the context of hospitalized patients' high risk.

claim: Immunological memory protects against infections by enabling a quicker and stronger immune response to a previously encountered antigen.
source: Immunological memory protects against infections by enabling a quicker and stronger immune response to a previously encountered antigen (Farber et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Immune memory is classically thought to be exclusively mediated by adaptive T and B cell responses.
source: Classically, immune memory is thought to be exclusively mediated by adaptive T and B cell responses.
evidence: This represents established scientific knowledge about classical immunology.

claim: Adaptive immune responses are highly specific to antigen, but take days or weeks to become effective.
source: These responses are highly specific to antigen, but take days or weeks to become effective.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the kinetics of adaptive immunity.

claim: Innate immune response provides an initial, relatively nonspecific response to infection within hours to days without immunological memory.
source: Another part of the immune system, innate immune response, provides an initial, relatively nonspecific response to infection within hours to days without immunological memory.
evidence: This represents classical understanding of innate immunity.

claim: Innate immune cells such as monocytes, macrophage, and NK cells can build long-term memory through epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of cells.
source: However, in the past decade, evidence has emerged showing that innate immune cells such as monocytes, macrophage, and NK cells can also build long-term memory through epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of cells.
evidence: This is stated as emerging evidence from the past decade, representing current scientific knowledge.

claim: Trained immunity produces hyperresponsiveness upon restimulation in innate immune cells.
source: This memory termed 'trained immunity' or 'trained innate immunity'' produces hyperresponsiveness upon restimulation in these cells (Netea et al., 2016; Netea and Joosten, 2018; Netea et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to three studies on trained immunity.

claim: All IWC-vaccinated mice survived when challenged 2 days or 7 days post immunization, whereas control mice succumbed to the infection.
source: The control mice succumbed to the infection, whereas all IWC-vaccinated mice survived when mice were challenged 2 days or 7 days post immunization (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B survival curves.

claim: Bacterial burdens in lungs and blood of vaccinated mice were significantly lower than those in the control group at 24 hr post infection.
source: Consistent with the survival rate, bacterial burdens in lungs and blood of vaccinated mice were significantly lower than those in the control group at 24 hr post infection (hpi; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: IWC-immunized mice showed reduced lung damage and decreased inflammatory cells infiltration.
source: Histopathology of lung tissues showed reduced lung damage and decreased inflammatory cells infiltration in IWC-immunized mice (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6 in lungs was significantly lower in IWC-vaccinated group than in control group at 24 hpi when challenging mice at day 7 post immunization.
source: When challenging the mice at day 7 post immunization, the pro-inflammatory cytokines of IL-6 in lungs (Figure 1E) and serum levels of IL-6 and TNF-α (Figure 1F) in the IWC-vaccinated group were significantly lower than those in the control group at 24 hpi.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Serum levels of IL-6 and TNF-α in the IWC-vaccinated group were significantly lower than those in the control group at 24 hpi.
source: When challenging the mice at day 7 post immunization, the pro-inflammatory cytokines of IL-6 in lungs (Figure 1E) and serum levels of IL-6 and TNF-α (Figure 1F) in the IWC-vaccinated group were significantly lower than those in the control group at 24 hpi.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Expression of chemokines Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl5, Cxcl10, and Ccl2 was significantly reduced in the lungs of vaccinated mice at 24 hpi.
source: Expression of chemokines Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl5, Cxcl10, and Ccl2 was also significantly reduced in the lungs of vaccinated mice at 24 hpi (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The number of neutrophils in lungs of vaccinated mice was significantly lower than that of control group at 24 hpi.
source: The results showed that the number of neutrophils in lungs of vaccinated mice was significantly lower than that of control group at 24 hpi (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1H.

claim: A single intranasal immunization with IWC of LAC-4 elicited rapid protection against pulmonary infection of clinical isolates SJZ24 and SJZ26.
source: The results showed that a single intranasal immunization with IWC of LAC-4 also elicited rapid protection against pulmonary infection of clinical isolates SJZ24 and SJZ26 (Figure 2A).

claim: Intranasal immunization of different strains of SJZ24, SJZ26, SJZ09, or ATCC17978 all induced rapid and effective protection against lethal LAC-4 infection.
source: These results showed that intranasal immunization of different strains of SJZ24, SJZ26, SJZ09, or ATCC17978 all induced rapid and effective protection against lethal LAC-4 infection (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B survival curves.

claim: SJZ24 is an extremely antibiotic-resistant clinical isolate.
source: SJZ24 is an extremely antibiotic-resistant clinical isolate (Zeng et al., 2019), LAC-4 is a MDR strain, and ATCC17978 is a reference strain which is an antibiotic-sensitive strain (Harris et al., 2013).

claim: LAC-4 is a MDR strain.
source: SJZ24 is an extremely antibiotic-resistant clinical isolate (Zeng et al., 2019), LAC-4 is a MDR strain, and ATCC17978 is a reference strain which is an antibiotic-sensitive strain (Harris et al., 2013).

claim: ATCC17978 is a reference strain which is an antibiotic-sensitive strain.
source: SJZ24 is an extremely antibiotic-resistant clinical isolate (Zeng et al., 2019), LAC-4 is a MDR strain, and ATCC17978 is a reference strain which is an antibiotic-sensitive strain (Harris et al., 2013).

claim: Intranasal immunization of IWC of A. baumannii can elicit broad protection against different clinical strains independent of drug resistance.
source: Together, these data suggested that intranasal immunization of IWC of A. baumannii can elicit broad protection against different clinical strains independent of drug resistance.

claim: Levels of TNF-α and IL-6 in lungs increased from day 1 to day 4 and completely declined to baseline by day 5 in response to intranasal immunization of IWC.
source: In response to intranasal immunization of IWC, levels of TNF-α and IL-6 in lungs increased from day 1 to day 4 and completely declined to baseline by day 5 (Figure 3A), indicating that the host response rapidly primed and rest 5 days later.

claim: TNF-α but not IL-6 and IL-1β levels was significantly higher in lungs from IWC-immunized mice than those from control mice at 2 hpi.
source: We found that TNF-α but not IL-6 and IL-1β levels was significantly higher in lungs from IWC-immunized mice than those from control mice (Figure 3B), suggesting that IWC-induced rapid TNF-α production might be responsible for the rapid protection.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IWC-induced rapid TNF-α production might be responsible for the rapid protection.
source: We found that TNF-α but not IL-6 and IL-1β levels was significantly higher in lungs from IWC-immunized mice than those from control mice (Figure 3B), suggesting that IWC-induced rapid TNF-α production might be responsible for the rapid protection.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the differential cytokine response observed.

claim: mRNA levels of Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl5, Cxcl10, and Ccl2 were higher in vaccinated mice than in control mice at early 2 hpi.
source: Further, mRNA levels of Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl5, Cxcl10, and Ccl2 were higher in vaccinated mice than in control mice at early 2 hpi (Figure 3C).

claim: Vaccinated mice had significantly higher numbers of neutrophils and monocytes in their lungs than did control mice at 4 hpi.
source: Meanwhile, consistent with the increased chemokine expression, vaccinated mice had significantly higher numbers of neutrophils and monocytes in their lungs than did control mice at 4 hpi (Figure 3D).

source: These results indicate that IWC immunization induces quick and enhanced responses upon A. baumannii challenge on day 7 after vaccination, which is an enhanced recall response of immune response.

source: Results showed that IWC provided rapid and effective protection both in WT and Rag1-/- mice at day 7 after immunization (Figure 4A).

source: There is no significant difference between WT and Rag1-/- mice in terms of survival of the IWC-immunized group (Figure 4A, p=0.30, log-rank test).

source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of DEGs revealed that genes associated with inflammatory response, response to molecule of bacterial origin, and response to liposaccharide were significantly downregulated in vaccinated mice at 24 hpi (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).

source: These results indicate that IWC immunization induces a trained feature of innate immune response, which is critical for vaccination-induced rapid protection.

evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstrated rapid protection via trained innate immunity.

claim: AMs are the predominant cells in the airway mucosa and play important roles for infection controls.
source: AMs are the predominant cells in the airway mucosa and play important roles for infection controls (Hussell and Bell, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hussell and Bell, 2014.

claim: The embryonic origin and the ability of self-renewal in steady state of AMs make them be able to store immune memory.
source: The embryonic origin and the ability of self-renewal in steady state of AMs make them be able to store immune memory (Hussell and Bell, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hussell and Bell, 2014.

claim: AMs could be trained to gain the memory phenotype in an adenovirus-infected models, which is dependent on IFN-γ production from effector CD8+ T cells.
source: It has been reported that AMs could be trained to gain the memory phenotype in an adenovirus-infected models, which is dependent on IFN-γ production from effector CD8+ T cells (Yao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yao et al., 2018.

claim: The trained feature of AMs can be manipulated to combat MDR bacterial pneumonia and also the respiratory virus infection.
source: The trained feature of AMs can be manipulated to combat MDR bacterial pneumonia and also the respiratory virus infection.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications based on the findings.

claim: A range of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), including Toll-like receptors (TLRs), nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 2 (NOD2), and dectin-1 might be engaged to promote trained immunity.
source: As for how AMs are trained, a range of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), including Toll-like receptors (TLRs), nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 2 (NOD2), and dectin-1 might be engaged to promote trained immunity.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on existing knowledge about trained immunity mechanisms.

claim: Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) and its main component muramyl dipeptide induce trained immunity through NOD2-ligand.
source: Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) and its main component muramyl dipeptide induce trained immunity through NOD2-ligand (Kleinnijenhuis et al., 2012) and β-glucan through dectin-1 receptor (Quintin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kleinnijenhuis et al., 2012.

claim: β-glucan induces trained immunity through dectin-1 receptor.
source: Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) and its main component muramyl dipeptide induce trained immunity through NOD2-ligand (Kleinnijenhuis et al., 2012) and β-glucan through dectin-1 receptor (Quintin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Quintin et al., 2012.

claim: Some studies have implicated that TLRs are upregulated to BCG or β-glucan training.
source: Some studies have implicated that TLRs are upregulated to BCG or β-glucan training (Kleinnijenhuis et al., 2012; Quintin et al., 2012); however, how TLRs are involved in trained immunity is not clear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to two studies.

claim: Elevated TLR4 expression on AMs might be a trained marker, which can sense the pathogen-associated molecular pattern more efficiently and results in rapid activation of trained AMs compared to naïve AMs.
source: These data suggest that elevated TLR4 expression on AMs might be a trained marker, which can sense the pathogen-associated molecular pattern more efficiently and results in rapid activation of trained AMs compared to naïve AMs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the TLR4 expression data and its functional consequences.

claim: TNF-α is critical for an effective antibacterial host defense against bacterial infection by regulating downstream cytokine response and activating immune cells.
source: TNF-α is critical for an effective antibacterial host defense against bacterial infection by regulating downstream cytokine response and activating immune cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TNF-α function.

claim: TNF-α is one of the main cytokines that has been thoroughly used as a functional cytokine marker indicating trained immunity along with IL-6 and IL-1β.
source: TNF-α is one of the main cytokines that has been thoroughly used as a functional cytokine marker indicating trained immunity along with IL-6 and IL-1β (Arts et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Arts et al., 2018.

claim: Vaccination-trained immune response produces heightened TNF-α, but not IL-6 and IL-1β, when encountered with the infection.

claim: Blocking TNF-α with specific antibody before challenge significantly reduces vaccine-induced rapid protection.

claim: Enhanced production of TNF-α from AMs is a functional indicator of trained AMs and is responsible for vaccine-elicited rapid protection.
source: These data collectively indicate that enhanced production of TNF-α from AMs is a functional indicator of trained AMs and is responsible for vaccine-elicited rapid protection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the combined data on TNF-α production and blocking experiments.

claim: The different cell wall component in Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria may account for the different vaccination effect of different bacteria.

source: In summary, in this study we demonstrate that intranasal immunization of IWC of certain bacteria induces a rapid, sufficient, and broad protection against lethal respiratory infection through inducing trained immunity of AMs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion summarizing the study findings.

claim: Exploiting the classical adaptive memory and trained innate immunity in an integrated fashion seems plausible for a potential good design of vaccination strategies against bacterial infection.

evidence: This is a speculative statement about future vaccine design strategies.
